overall: Los Angeles is starting June 25 under classic June Gloom conditions, with temperatures locked in a flat overnight range of 62–62.6°F and no meaningful warming trend evident through 05:00 ET. A persistent marine layer is producing patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies, keeping dewpoints elevated (~57°F) and suppressing any early-morning heating. The NWS forecast of 'near 69°F' aligns with the broader model consensus, suggesting a modest afternoon warm-up once the fog burns off around midday.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in reasonable agreement, clustering between 67.0°F (NBM) and 69.8°F (HRRR), with ECMWF at 68.2°F — a ~2.8°F spread that is fairly tight for this time of day. The HRRR is the bullish outlier, pushing near 70°F, while the NBM anchors the low end at 67°F. The current observed running max of 62.6°F is entirely consistent with a marine-layer morning that hasn't yet begun to heat, so no significant departure from model guidance is apparent at this early hour.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence — NWS text forecast of 69°F, HRRR at 69.8°F, ECMWF at 68.2°F, and NBM at 67.0°F — points to a daily high in the 68–69°F range. Mostly cloudy skies and lingering fog through mid-morning will limit solar insolation during the critical early heating window, slightly favoring the lower end of the model spread (closer to ECMWF/NBM than HRRR). Confidence is moderate; the 68–69°F bucket is the most likely landing zone, with meaningful probability (~19%) that temps push into the 70–71°F range if the marine layer clears earlier or more completely than forecast.
